Fraud removal is essential, but let’s not pretend the Big Beautiful Bill stops there. The CBO projects $2.4-$5.8T added to the deficit, with Medicaid cuts targeting 4.5M children’s health coverage and SNAP restrictions risking 2M kids’ food assistance. Section 203(b) slashes $300B from nutrition programs under the guise of “eligibility checks” while preserving corporate farm subsidies.

The House version’s $1.6T in cuts disproportionately hit working families—20M children get partial/no child tax credit due to income thresholds. Real reform would audit pharma overcharges in Medicare (saving $200B/yr) instead of squeezing vulnerable Americans.

Protect the safety net, but this bill’s structure prioritizes optics over outcomes.
